DILG OPINION No. L- VICE MAYOR EDITO A.G. BALINTONA 1 e JAN Municipality of Sarrat Province of Ilocos Norte Dear Vice-Mayor Balintona: This has reference to your letter dated 31 July 2017 requesting for this Department's legal opinion whether the Municipal Administrator who is tasked to man the office of the Mayor may officiate or conduct a marriage ceremony in the absence of the local chief executive (LCE) for not more than three (3) days. First and foremost, we agree with you that a Vice-Mayor, in his capacity as Acting Mayor can validly solemnize marriage based on the herein-quoted provision of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code (LGC), specifically Article 83(d), which provides for an "Acting Capacity", to wit: "Temporary incapacity — When the governor, city or municipal mayor, orpunong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice governor, city or municipal vice mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. " Anent your query, before we answer the same, it is worthy to know first the distinction of an "Acting Capacity" and an "Officer-in-charge" (OIC). In Resolution No. 0007778 dated 24 March 2000, issued by the Civil Service Commission (CSC), re: "Distinction between Acting and OIC", it was pointed out that: "It must be noted that a designation under acting capacity may be differentiated from a designation as Officer-in-Charge (OIC) in such a manner that an OIC enjoys limited powers which are confined to functions of administration and ensuring that the office continues its usual activities. The OIC may not be deemed to possess the power to s. 2012

0) appoint employees as the same involves the exercise ofdiscretion which is beyond the power of an OIC On the other hand, as aptly ruled by the Commission in the case of Amado S. Day, a designation in an acting capacity entails not only the exercise of the ministerial functions attached to the position but also the exercise of discretion. " "The designation of an OIC is nothing more than a temporary and convenient arrangement intended to avert paralyzation of the day to day operations of an office in the meantime that the chief or head of office is temporarily absent. " It can be gleaned from the above-quoted CSC Resolution that functions of an OIC is purely ministerial. Further, in the case of Eligio Mallari vs. Banco Filipino Savings and Mortgagel, it was held that: "The distinction between a ministerial and discretionary act is well delineated. A purely ministerial act or duty is one which an officer or tribunal performs in a given state of facts, in a prescribed manner, in obedience to the mandate ofa legal authority, without regard to or the exercise of his own judgment upon the propriety or impropriety of the act done. Ifthe law imposes a duty upon a public officer and gives him the right to decide how or when the duty shall be performed, such duty is discretionary and not ministerial. The duty is ministerial only when the discharge of the same requires neither the exercise of ofFcia1 discretion or judgment. " In your letter, it appears that the (LCE) travels outside of his jurisdiction for not more than 3 days. Clearly, the designation contemplated in your letter is designation as OIC and it is governed by Article 83(d)(3)(i) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code (LGC), which states that: "When the incumbent local chief executive is traveling within the country but outside his territorial jurisdiction for a period not exceeding three (3) consecutive days, he may designate in writing the officer-in-charge of the office of the local chief executive. Such authorization shall specify the powers and functions that the local official concerned shall exercise in the absence of the local chief executive except the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees. " Given the above discussion, it is clear that the duties of the OIC should be specified and should be limited only to the functions of administration as not to paralyze the day to day operations of the office. 1 GR No. 157660, 29 August 2008

Accordingly, the Department is of the considered view that officials designated as OICs have no authority to solemnize marriages as the same is not within the scope of the functions pertaining to administration of an office. CC: We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authorit f the Secretary: AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary 2018-0 RD James F. Fadrilan Regional Director Region I- Ilocos Region
